subject: SIG + privacy alignment: EU transfers, BAA feasibility, and next steps

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: SIG + GDPR / BAA questions for Redwood (MedSysCo evaluation)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is impressed. We are moving toward a vendor security review and have a few immediate items before procurement can proceed: 

- Can Redwood sign a BAA for covered health data stored/processed in our account?
- For EU data subjects, do you rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or an adequacy mechanism? Are SCCs available for customers in our region (UK/EU)?
- Please provide a completed SIG questionnaire (SIG-Lite or SIG) and any SOC 2 Type II evidence you can share under an NDA.

We are on a tight timeline to present to our InfoSec and legal teams next week. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? If helpful, CCing our DPO and Legal.

Best,
Emily

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 +0530
Subject: Re: SIG + GDPR / BAA questions for Redwood (MedSysCo evaluation)

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads and can sign a BAA for customers who meet the technical onboarding requirements. We have a standard BAA template we can share (and can negotiate limited redlines).
- EU transfers: We offer SCCs for customers; we also support region pins and residency for certain plans.
- SIG / SOC 2: We can deliver a completed SIG (we usually provide a SIG-Lite first, then full SIG on request) and our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.

I will loop in Security & Trust and Legal for evidence and to coordinate the BAA. ETA: I can share SIG-Lite responses and our draft BAA by Monday EOD (PST), SOC 2 report under NDA within 48 hours of NDA execution.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha will attach the SIG draft and SOC 2 placeholder.
2) If MedSysCo needs the full SIG, we will schedule a walkthrough with your DPO.
3) If you want to review BAA redlines, send to legal@redwood.ai and cc me.

Thanks — and happy to hop on a sync.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

- Monica: check our BAA template and any recent negotiated clauses (we had two enterprise BAAs in Q2). Add context on timelines for signing and redline turnaround.
- Jonas: FYI in case product-level constraints pop up on residency / region pin.

Keep Emily in loop; aim to have attachments and links by Monday EOD PST.

Priyom

Priyom / team / Emily — attaching the items below. Short summary included.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_SIG_Response_v1.pdf (SIG-Lite responses; marked in-scope / out-of-scope where appropriate)
- Redwood_BAA_Template_v2.docx (our standard BAA with a short redline history in the cover sheet)
- SOC2_Type2_Redwood-2025.pdf (redacted SOC 2 Type II; available under click-through NDA)

Summary notes:
- SCCs: We issue the EU Commission-approved SCCs for customers requiring them. Implementation notes: SCCs are applied by addendum to the DPA; no additional infra changes required. For UK customers we use UK Addendum.
- BAA: We will sign a BAA. Typical exceptions we see: customer-side data residency guarantees and specific HSPD/air-gapped requirements (those can require private deployment). BAA turnaround: 1-2 business days for our standard template, additional time if extensive redlines.
- SOC 2: The redacted report attached covers controls through 2025. Full report access requires our standard NDA (link below).

Links:
- SIG answers folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_sig_answers
- SOC2 access: https://redwood.example.com/secure/soc2-report/2025 (click-through NDA)

If MedSysCo wants a full SIG (not SIG-Lite), we can scope that and schedule a 30–45 minute walkthrough with their DPO and our Security team this week.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Trust & Compliance

Neha — thanks, this is helpful and aligned with what we need. A few follow-ups: 

1) We'll review the SIG-Lite and SOC 2 link. Can you confirm whether the SOC 2 report includes encryption-in-transit and at-rest controls details, and whether key management is customer or Redwood-managed (KMS/HSM)?
2) For the BAA, our legal team will send a couple of minor redlines. Can you confirm who on Redwood Legal to expect that from so we can route directly?
3) Are SCCs implemented automatically, or do we need to sign a separate DPA addendum to apply them? Please confirm the effective date and reference to the SCC version.

Also — let's schedule a short call with our DPO to walk the SIG responses. Availability here: Wed 4pm BST or Thu 10am BST. Which works for Redwood?

Best,
Emily
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG + GDPR / BAA questions — attachments and evidence links

Emily — quick answers inline and we can pick Thu 10am BST for the walkthrough.

1) SOC 2: the redacted report includes control mappings for encryption-in-transit and encryption-at-rest (AES-256). Key management: by default, Redwood manages keys in our KMS, but we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated and Private deployments — note that customer KMS requires additional onboarding steps.

2) BAA legal contact: please send redlines to legal@redwood.ai and cc me. Monica will lead the review; she is copied.

3) SCCs: SCCs are applied via DPA addendum. We use the current EU Commission SCCs and the UK addendum where applicable. Effective date is the execution date of the DPA addendum — Neha has included a link and the text reference in the SIG answers folder.

Call: Thu 10:00 BST works for Redwood (that's 11:00 CEST / 06:00 PDT). I'll invite our DPO and product privacy lead.

Next steps: Neha to confirm SOC 2 click-through availability for MedSysCo (she already provided the link) and Monica to acknowledge receipt of legal redlines when they come in.

Thanks — speak Thursday.

Priyom
